sections.h2: Where is Lafayette, Louisiana, and what is the land like?
sections.html:
Lafayette is a city of about 121,000 people on the Vermilion River in the Acadiana region of south Louisiana. The 2020 census counted 121,374 residents, which made it the state's fourth most populous city, and the city covers 55.65 square miles of almost entirely dry land.

It lies roughly 59 miles from Baton Rouge, 75 miles from Lake Charles and 135 miles from New Orleans, at an elevation of 36 to 49 feet above sea level. The ground belongs to the southwestern Louisiana Prairie Terrace, which sits higher than the wetlands to the south and west.

According to Wikipedia's summary of the city, Lafayette does not have significant flooding problems apart from local flash flooding. Drainage runs through natural channels including Isaac Verot Coulee, Coulee Mine, Coulee des Poches and Coulee Ile des Cannes, all of which lead to the Vermilion. A seller whose lot backs onto a coulee should expect buyers to ask about drainage and flood insurance.

sections.h2: What is the history behind the city?
sections.html:
Lafayette began as Vermilionville. Jean Mouton, an Acadian settler, gave land for a small Catholic chapel, the site was chosen as the parish seat in 1824, and the Legislature approved incorporation in 1836. The town took the name Lafayette in 1884.

Agriculture, mainly sugar, carried the local economy into the early twentieth century. The university that is now the University of Louisiana at Lafayette was established in 1898 and opened in 1901. Oil was found in the parish in the 1940s, and by 2018 Lafayette had the largest number of oil and natural gas workers in the state.

The city and parish governments consolidated in 1996. Voters split the single council into a city council and a parish council in 2018, though the mayor-president is still elected parishwide. Lafayette Consolidated Government runs public works and land use for the city and for unincorporated areas.

Energy, health care, education and retail carry the local job market. Wikipedia lists the consolidated city-parish's top employers as of 2021 as the Lafayette Parish School System, Lafayette General Health, Wood Group Production Services, Lafayette Consolidated Government, the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, WHC Inc., Walmart, Our Lady of Lourdes Regional Medical Center, Schlumberger and Stuller Inc.

The area has also become a center for technology, aerospace and banking. That mix helps sellers in two ways. Hospital and university jobs steady housing demand, but a downturn in oil activity can slow it, so timing and certainty of closing matter to anyone selling a house under pressure.

  • Education: the Lafayette Parish School System runs 45 schools, and the University of Louisiana at Lafayette enrolls more than 18,000 students.
  • Community college: South Louisiana Community College is headquartered in the city.
  • Health care: Lafayette General Health joined Ochsner Health, and Our Lady of Lourdes is a major regional hospital.

sections.h2: What is Lafayette's climate, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Lafayette has a humid subtropical climate with rain in every season and heavy summer humidity. NOAA normals for Lafayette Regional Airport show about 62.81 inches of precipitation a year on 117.5 days with measurable rain, and July and August average daily highs above 91 degrees.

The record high is 110 degrees on August 27, 2023, and the record low is 4 degrees on January 22, 2025, so air conditioning and pipe protection both get tested. For a house, that means roofs, attic ventilation, HVAC age and moisture damage are the usual inspection topics.

An older home with a tired roof or a failing compressor can scare off financed buyers, because lenders and appraisers flag those items. Sellers in that position often weigh whether to spend on repairs or sell as-is.

sections.h2: How do you get around Lafayette?
sections.html:
Interstate 10 and Interstate 49 are the main highways, and U.S. 90 and U.S. 167 cross the city under street names such as Evangeline Thruway, Johnston Street and Cameron Street. Ambassador Caffery Parkway forms a partial loop connecting I-10 at Exit 100 on the west with U.S. 90 on the south.

Lafayette Regional Airport is on the southeast side and has scheduled nonstop service to Atlanta, Dallas/Fort Worth, Houston and Charlotte. A new passenger terminal opened on January 20, 2022. The city summary also lists Amtrak's Sunset Limited, which runs three days a week between New Orleans and Los Angeles.

Access to the interstate and to the university and hospital districts shapes which neighborhoods move fastest, and a buyer's commute is one of the first questions a seller hears.

sections.h2: How is city property tax billed in Lafayette?
sections.html:
City tax is billed separately from parish tax. Lafayette Consolidated Government mails city notices at the end of November, and they are delinquent after December 31. After that date the city adds 1% interest per month, and a penalty starts in February.

The city does not accept partial payments, so the full assessment has to be paid at once. You can pay online, walk in at 2701 Moss Street between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays, or mail a payment to P.O. Box 4024-C, Lafayette, LA 70502. Cash, check or money order are taken in person, with checks made out to Lafayette Consolidated Government.

Parish taxes are collected by the Sheriff's Office, whose web tax site accepts e-check and major credit cards for a transaction fee. A Lafayette homeowner therefore often holds two bills. Ask your closing agent to confirm both are current before the act of sale.

sections.h2: What happens at the Lafayette tax sale?
sections.html:
The city and parish tax sale takes place online on the first Wednesday in June, and the list is published in the local newspaper on the two Sundays before it.

A home with unpaid taxes that nobody buys at the sheriff's sale becomes adjudicated. Lafayette's adjudicated property FAQ explains that such a property is not owned by the city or parish, and that it has to be adjudicated for three consecutive years before the government will process an application. At any point before the act of sale is recorded, the owner can still redeem by paying all taxes, liens and fees to both collectors.

That redemption right is why selling early is usually cheaper. Each month of delay adds 1% interest and the risk of losing control of the property.

sections.h2: What local code rules should a Lafayette seller know about?
sections.html:
Lafayette Consolidated Government handles property maintenance complaints through its Environmental Quality Division at 337-291-8500, covering long grass, solid waste, hazardous materials and overgrowth. Dilapidated structures go to the Compliance Division at 337-291-8445.

Vacant or inherited houses attract those complaints quickly. Clearing the yard and boarding hazards before listing, or selling to a buyer who takes the property in its current condition, avoids a code notice arriving while you are under contract.

Louisiana does not treat a sale as complete against outsiders until the deed is recorded with the Clerk of Court, so a closing is not done when you sign, only when the act of sale is filed. Our Lafayette Parish clerk guide covers that step in detail.

faqs.q: What is the Lafayette property tax due date?
faqs.a: City notices go out at the end of November and become delinquent after December 31. The parish bill is collected separately by the Sheriff, whose published deadline without penalty is also December 31.

faqs.q: Does Lafayette charge interest on late taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Lafayette Consolidated Government adds 1% interest per month after December 31, and a penalty starts in February. Partial payments are not accepted on city taxes.

faqs.q: When is the Lafayette tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held online on the first Wednesday in June. The tax sale list is published in the local newspaper on the two Sundays before the sale.

Wikipedia's city summary says Lafayette sits on higher prairie terrace and has no significant flooding apart from local flash flooding, with natural coulees carrying water to the Vermilion River. Check the flood zone for a specific lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lafayette house with unpaid city taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid city and parish taxes are paid from the sale proceeds. A buyer who closes as-is can handle a sale with taxes owed.
